# Scope

All pages were read on 2026-11-12. Base URL for documentation: `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/` (cited below as `docs:<page>.md`). Values follow `protocol.md` version 1. "Availability" is the vendor's own label where a page gives one; "no label" means the page states plan or version requirements and no preview label.

One reading rule I applied and disclose: when a feature carries out a service's full definition on one surface only (cloud sessions only, or local sessions only), I rate **yes** and name the surface in the Availability column.

| Sessions | yes | "Each message, tool use, and result is written to a plaintext JSONL file under `~/.claude/projects/`, which enables rewinding, resuming, and forking sessions." Grant: decision source "A grant for the rest of the session, given at an earlier permission prompt" (docs:monitoring-usage.md). | docs:permissions.md | No label |

Record: `tool_decision` event "Logged when a tool permission decision is made (accept/reject)" (docs:monitoring-usage.md). | docs:permissions.md | No label; the event record needs telemetry export turned on |
| Observability | yes | "OpenTelemetry events are the audit data source for Claude Code activity." Also the session transcript (see Sessions). | docs:monitoring-usage.md | No label; "Traces (beta)" |
| Evaluation | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | "The `claude plugin eval` shell command runs your plugin against a suite of test cases and scores the results." Also "`/goal` adds a separate evaluator that checks your condition after every turn" (docs:goal.md). Reason: a run that could not be graded is scored as a failure, not as unknown: "Such a run scores 0 with no grader results, and the command exits non-zero". Yes is defensible because the result marks runs that are not comparable: "`partial` ... `true` with `cost_ceiling`, `interrupted`, or `auth_failed` when the suite didn't finish". | docs:plugin-evals.md | No label ("general availability of the command" is referred to); needs v2.1.269 |
| Improvement | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Claude looks for problems such as instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. You get a report of findings with proposed edits" (`/doctor prompt-audit`, docs:memory.md). `/insights` "analyzes your recent sessions on this machine and writes an HTML report covering ... friction points ... and suggestions for using Claude Code more effectively" (docs:costs.md). Reason: proposals come from file audits, usage statistics and session reports that the user asks for; I found no feature that turns evaluations or reviews into proposed changes to agents or the platform, except the optional `skill-creator` plugin, which "proposes description edits" (docs:skills.md). | docs:memory.md | No label; `/doctor prompt-audit` needs v2.1.283 |
| Releases | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Claude Code has no release-channel concept, and one marketplace serves one version of each plugin at a time." Reason: plugins carry versions and auto-update, and a way back exists only as a pinned git ref the marketplace host manages ("append `#<ref>`"). The product itself has channels and a downgrade path: "`"stable"`: use a version that is typically about one week old" (docs:setup.md). I found nothing that versions or releases rules or infrastructure. Yes is defensible on plugin versions plus the product's own release channels. | docs:plugins/host-marketplace.md | No label |
| Reliability | yes | "Exited unexpectedly while the supervisor is running: the supervisor restarts the process." "Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff" (docs:errors.md). "Claude Code reconnects a remote server that drops mid-session" (docs:mcp.md). Limit stated by the vendor: "Shutting down or restarting your machine stops running background sessions." | docs:agent-view.md | Supervisor: "research preview". Retries and reconnection: no label |

Counts: yes 19, part 5, no 1. Six cells are marked DISPUTABLE, each with the next value up as the alternative: Memory, Identity, Evaluation, Improvement and Releases (part, alternative yes) and Directory (no, alternative part).

# Further question 1: areas of work (C1 to C4, rerate-criteria-v2)

Unit rated: the **Project** (Projects feature). Other candidate units and why I did not rate them higher: an agent team ("one session that starts teammate sessions for a single task ... and ends with that task", docs:claude-projects.md) is one team for one task; a plugin is a packaging unit ("installs and loads as one unit"); the organization is the whole system.

| Criterion | Value | Quote and reason | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | "A project is one ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates a stream of related work for you." "Starting a project from scratch means opening the **New project** dialog, naming the stream of work, and optionally giving it a goal and the repositories and files it works on." Reason for part: the vendor defines the unit as one coordinating conversation and the threads it starts, which reads as one team of agents, and version 2 rules out a unit that models a conversation. Yes is defensible: the unit has stated properties (name, goal, instructions, memory, repositories, environment), several sessions belong to it, and a user can hold several projects ("how the project appears in the **Projects** list"; "You can't merge two projects into one"). | docs:claude-projects.md, sections "How a project is organized", "Start a new project from scratch", "Limitations" |
| C2 | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | (a) is met at the unit level: "one line that becomes the project's goal, such as "Hold p95 API latency under 200 ms"". (b): the only positions are the fixed coordinator and worker: "one long-running session where Claude acts as coordinator"; "Threads: the workers". Reason for part: these two positions are the same in every project and are not roles specified for the area. Yes is defensible because they are positions defined apart from the session that fills them ("Coordinator model and effort", "Thread model and effort"). | docs:claude-projects.md, sections "Start a new project from scratch", "How a project is organized", "Project settings reference" |
| C3 | part | "`owner` ... Maintainer information. `name` is required" in `marketplace.json`, and `author` per plugin ("`name`, which is required, plus optional `email` and `url`"). Reason: a catalog names a maintainer per marketplace and an author per plugin; accountability is not stated and the entry is not per responsibility. No other ownership record found (search terms as in the Directory row). | docs:plugins/marketplace-reference.md; docs:plugins/manifest-reference.md |
| C4 | part. DISPUTABLE (yes) | "When Claude encounters a task that matches a subagent's description, it delegates to that subagent"; `ListAgents` "Lists the agents Claude can message with `SendMessage`". Reason for part: the match from a kind of work happens inside the delegating session's own context, and the cross-session listing is a list of sessions, not a lookup from a kind of work. Yes is defensible because subagent definitions with a required `description` ("When Claude should delegate to this subagent") are a defined element that any session loads. | docs:sub-agents.md; docs:tools-reference.md |

Derived Directory by the rule in rerate-criteria-v2: **part** (C3 part, C4 part).

# Further question 2: supplied agents, roles or skills for a named area of work

Software engineering (in the product):
- Built-in subagents Explore ("A fast, read-only agent optimized for searching and analyzing codebases"), Plan ("codebase research for planning") and general-purpose. docs:sub-agents.md
- Bundled skills: "Claude Code includes a set of bundled skills, such as `/doctor`, `/code-review`, `/batch`, `/debug`, `/loop`, and `/claude-api`"; also `/security-review`, `/simplify`, `/verify`. docs:skills.md; docs:commands.md
- Code Review: "Several agents read each change alongside the surrounding code". "For Team and Enterprise plans". docs:code-review.md
- Claude Security plugin: "runs a multi-agent vulnerability scan of your codebase inside a Claude Code session". docs:claude-security.md
- Official marketplace: "Anthropic maintains a smaller set of its own, such as `commit-commands`, `code-review`, `feature-dev`". docs:plugins/anthropic-marketplaces.md

Research: "Claude Code includes `/deep-research` as a built-in workflow". docs:workflows.md

Other areas (Anthropic's `knowledge-work-plugins` marketplace, added by the user): "Each plugin bundles the skills, connectors, slash commands, and sub-agents for a specific job function." "Built for Claude Cowork, also compatible with Claude Code." Eleven plugins: productivity, sales, customer-support, product-management, marketing, legal, finance, data, enterprise-search, bio-research, cowork-plugin-management. https://github.com/anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins (README), named in docs:plugins/anthropic-marketplaces.md as a "topic-specific" marketplace.

# Further question 3: what fits nowhere

- Spend metering and caps. "Spend limits cap how much each developer can spend through your Claude apps gateway in a given day, week, or month." docs:claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits.md. Also `--max-budget-usd` "Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls" (`claude --help`) and `/usage` (docs:commands.md). Closest services are Policy and Observability; neither names cost.
- Undo of an agent's changes to the workspace. "Claude Code automatically tracks Claude's file edits as you work, allowing you to quickly undo changes and rewind to previous states". docs:checkpointing.md. Releases covers a way back for released changes, not for a session's edits.
- Changing the product's own interface. "A mod is a plugin that changes how Claude Code looks and behaves." docs:plugins/mods/overview.md
- Onboarding people. `/team-onboarding`: "Generate a team onboarding guide from your Claude Code usage history." docs:commands.md

# Further question 4: where it runs and what the user supplies

Where it runs: both. "Local: Your machine ... Cloud: Anthropic-managed VMs, or self-hosted environments your organization operates ... Remote Control: Your machine, controlled from a browser". docs:how-claude-code-works.md

When the user is away:
- Cloud: "The session keeps running after you close your laptop, and you can check on it or steer it from any device." docs:claude-code-on-the-web.md
- Local background sessions: "Background sessions don't need any terminal open to keep working." and "Sessions are local: background sessions run on your machine. They are preserved across sleep but stop if the machine shuts down." docs:agent-view.md
- Projects: "Cloud threads keep going after you close your laptop, while a thread on your computer runs only while that computer is awake." docs:claude-projects.md
- Chat channels: "Events only arrive while the session is open, so for an always-on setup you run Claude in a background process or persistent terminal." docs:channels.md

What the user supplies or builds:
- An account: "Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, or Console account." docs:setup.md
- For cloud sessions, a code host connection: "To let cloud sessions clone your code from GitHub and push branches, connect GitHub". docs:claude-code-on-the-web.md
- The standing instructions and extensions: "features you add to customize what Claude knows, connect it to external services, and automate workflows" (CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP, subagents, hooks, plugins). docs:features-overview.md
- For a chat channel, its credentials: "You install a channel as a plugin and configure it with your own credentials." docs:channels.md
- For sustained local work, the machine that stays on (quotes above). I found no accountability record and no agent that persists with its own identity in the pages read; a user who wants those builds them from the parts above.

# Disclosures and what could not be opened

- Pages were fetched as Markdown with curl. Long pages were read by heading and keyword, not line by line, so a feature described only in a section I did not reach could be missed. This matters most for the **no** on Directory and for the absence statements in Memory, Identity, Improvement and Releases.
- `docs:claude-tag.md` returned an HTML page for `claude.com/docs/claude-tag` instead of Markdown. I did not read the Claude Tag documentation. Claude Tag (Claude in Slack channels for Team and Enterprise, with an organization "shared identity") is described by the vendor as differing from Claude Code and is not rated here. If it is counted as part of Claude Code, Identity and Channels should be read again.
- Not opened: claude.ai admin and settings pages (sign-in required), support.claude.com articles, platform.claude.com API references (routines fire endpoint, Compliance API, Workload Identity Federation), claude.com/marketplace, the Anthropic blog posts the prompt library links to, and the plugin repositories other than the one README above.
- No Claude Code session was started, no prompt was sent, and no configuration was changed.
- No file under `` was opened other than `protocol.md` and `rerate-criteria-v2.md`, and no search printed content from one.
- The reader is itself a Claude Code subagent. Its own tool list and the project instructions loaded into its context describe a Claude Code deployment; none of that was used as evidence. Every value rests on the pages listed.
- Availability labels are the vendor's. Several rows rest on features labeled research preview (agent view, cloud scheduled tasks, channels), public beta (Projects, self-hosted environments) or experimental (agent teams); a reader who rates preview features lower would change Tasks, Scheduling and Lifecycle.
